```text
# #4418: Patch: follow-up to #4411 from the after-merge spot-check
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

<!-- jackioh-bot:spot-check-follow-up #4411 -->
The after-merge spot-check of #4411 ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/44945953883)) found 2 blocking problem(s) in the change as it merged (`4521cdf8a4a3`). `claude-1` (claude, `opus`, strong) reviewed it. #4411 stays merged: nothing is reverted, and this issue fixes what it found in a change of its own, from `main`.

## What to fix

- [ ] `crates/server/src/api/settings.rs:237`: The account's stored cosmetics group is read with a plain select before the merge takes its profile row lock, so a concurrent write by a second device can be undone: the refused key is put back to the value from before that device's write, not the value stored when this write merges. The issue named this risk and asked for the read to be taken under the profile lock or for the race to be shown harmless; the PR's claim that reading in the same transaction settles it is wrong.
  Evidence: put_settings calls tx.player_settings_get, which is pg.rs:4389-4406: `select … from public.player_settings where profile_id = $1::uuid`, with no `for update`. Only after that does player_settings_merge call app.merge_player_settings, which takes the lock inside the SQL function (migration 0018: 'Under the profile row lock (`select ... for update`)'). pg.rs begin sets no isolation level, so Postgres runs at the default read committed. The race: device B sends {table: unowned} at t2 and reads held {table: W}. Device A then commits {table: X} at t1 < t2. B's merge stores {table: W} at t2, so A's X is reverted to W, which contradicts R4403000's 'the key keeps the value the account's stored cosmetics group already holds'. The fake store (fake.rs:495, `data.lock().await` held for the whole transaction) runs every transaction one at a time, so no test can catch this. Fix: read the held row under the lock, with a `for update` read of player_settings or of the profile row before the filter, or apply the keep inside app.merge_player_settings. Add a store contract test or a pg-suite test for it.
- [ ] `spec/rulings/R1834001.md:3`: R1834001 is amended by R4403000 but was left untouched. Its title has no 'amended by R4403000', and its body still says without qualification that a failing settings pick is 400 and 'nothing in the request is written', which is now false for NotOwned, with nothing in the note pointing a reader to the newer rule.
  Evidence: The amended notes follow a consistent convention: R1834001's title says '(… amended by R2655000)', R0634's says '(amended by R1758000)', and R1295000's says 'amended by R1655000, R1834001, R1834003, R1834004 and R2721000'. The diff adds R4403000 ('amends R1834001') but does not change R1834001.md, whose text reads 'A pick that fails is 400 `bad_request`, and nothing in the request is written.' The fix is to add 'amended by R4403000' to R1834001's title, and a pointer in its paragraph on failing picks.

## Done when

- Each finding above is fixed where it points, or answered with the evidence that it does not hold.
- Every check is green, with no test skipped, ignored or weakened to get there (CLAUDE.md rule 12).

---
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot from the after-merge spot-check (one in 5 medium or hard merges, `spot_check_every`): `muse` (`muse`) built #4411 and `muse` (`muse-spark-1.3-contributor`) approved it. This issue's own pull request is never spot-checked.

<!-- jackioh-bot -->

<!-- jackioh-bot:plan -->
## Plan

_Written by `muse` (muse, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/44946969302)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

Fix the two spot-check findings of #4411 without reverting it: close the lost-update race where `PUT /api/settings` reads the held `cosmetics` group before taking the profile lock, so a concurrent device's write can be reverted (violating R4403000's keep rule); and amend the R1834001 note, which R4403000 amends, so its title and failing-pick paragraph point at the newer rule. Done is the race closed in code, both notes consistent, and every named check green.

## Files to touch

| File | New / change | What changes there |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/server/src/db/store.rs` | change | New port method `Tx::player_settings_get_for_update` beside `player_settings_get` |
| `crates/server/src/db/pg.rs` | change | New `player_settings_get_for_update` with `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` |
| `crates/server/src/db/fake.rs` | change | New `player_settings_get_for_update`, same lookup as the fake's `player_settings_get` |
| `crates/server/src/api/settings.rs` | change | `put_settings` reads the held row through the locking method |
| `crates/server/tests/store/contract.rs` | change | New `r4403000_…` test in `mod player_settings`, registered in `both_stores!` |
| `spec/rulings/R1834001.md` | change | Title gains `and R4403000`; `cards` gains `R4403000`; failing-pick paragraph points at R4403000 |
| `spec/rulings/R4403000.md` | change | `proven_in` gains `crates/server/tests/store/contract.rs` |

Do not touch: anything under `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/` or `bot/`; `crates/server/migrations/` (no migration: the fix stays in the API/store layer); `spec/11-rulings.md`, `spec/INDEX.md`, `spec/CARDS.md` (the daily fold owns them); `spec/pending/` (no new ruling, so no new paragraph); any other crate or app. Governing spec: §9.1, R633, R634, R1834001, R4403000.

## Steps

1. In `spec/rulings/R1834001.md`, change the title to end `amended by R2655000 and R4403000)`, following the R1295000/R0634 convention of listing every amending ruling. Add `R4403000` to `cards` after `R1834002` (ascending order, as the list reads).
2. In the same note, qualify the failing-pick paragraph that now reads `A pick that fails is 400 bad_request, and nothing in the request is written.` Append a second sentence naming the exception with a link, e.g. `A cosmetics pick refused as NotOwned on PUT /api/settings is the exception: [[R4403000]] keeps it out of the write instead, holding the account's stored pick for the key.` Leave the rest of the note byte-identical.
3. In `spec/rulings/R4403000.md`, append `crates/server/tests/store/contract.rs` to `proven_in` (step 6 adds an `r4403000` test there, and `proven_in` must list every file that proves the ruling).
4. In `crates/server/src/db/store.rs`, directly after `player_settings_get`, add the port method with a doc comment citing the reason:
   `pub async fn player_settings_get_for_update(&mut self, profile_id: &str) -> StoreResult<Option<PlayerSettingsRow>>` dispatching via `dispatch!(self, player_settings_get_for_update(profile_id))`. Document: the locked read `put_settings` uses before its keep-out filter (R4403000, #4418); the lock is held until the transaction commits, so the later `player_settings_merge` in the same transaction cannot commit over a row this read did not see.
5. In `crates/server/src/db/pg.rs`, directly after `player_settings_get`, add `pub async fn player_settings_get_for_update` as a copy of that function (same `is_uuid` guard, same `run_as(t, Some(profile_id))`, same `player_settings_columns!()` and row mapping) with ` for update` appended to the `where` clause: `… from public.player_settings where profile_id = $1::uuid for update`. Copy the `R634` doc-comment style and note it takes the settings row lock so the filter reads what the merge will merge.
6. In `crates/server/src/db/fake.rs`, directly after `player_settings_get`, add the sync `pub fn player_settings_get_for_update(f: &mut FakeTx<'_>, profile_id: &str)` with hook name `"playerSettings.getForUpdate"` and the identical table lookup. Comment that the fake holds its one lock for the whole transaction, so this is already serial (the divergence the issue notes), and the method exists so both stores expose the same locked entry point.
7. In `crates/server/src/api/settings.rs` `put_settings`, replace only the held-row read (`tx.player_settings_get(&profile.id).await?` at line 238) with `tx.player_settings_get_for_update(&profile.id).await?`, plus a one-line comment that the held cosmetics are now read under the row lock the merge takes. Do not change `filter_cosmetics_group`, the merge call, or `get_settings` (which keeps the plain read).
8. In `crates/server/tests/store/contract.rs` `mod player_settings`, add `async fn r4403000_a_locked_read_answers_what_the_merge_just_left(harness: &StoreHarness)`: assert the locked read is `None` before the first write; `write` an `audio` group; assert the locked read in a new transaction equals the merged row and equals the plain `player_settings_get`. Register it in that module's `both_stores!` list. Reuse the existing `active_profile`, `write`, `merged`, `q!` helpers; no new helpers.

## Tests

- `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server_store r4403000` — the new contract test (memory half runs; the Postgres half self-skips without `DATABASE_URL`, CI runs it).
- `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server r4403000` and `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server r1834001` — the existing API keep-out/refusal tests still prove the behavior.
- `cargo fmt --check`; `cargo clippy -p jackioh-server --all-targets -- -D warnings`; `cargo jackioh spec check` (after the note edits; never run `spec index`).
- The Docker suites (`crates/server/tests/db/run.sh`, `tests/sql/run.sh`) stay CI's; do not run whole-workspace suites.

## Done when

- [ ] `put_settings`' held-cosmetics read goes through the `FOR UPDATE` port method, so a concurrent device's committed write is seen, never reverted, per R4403000's keep sentence; the no-row-yet case still leaves the key out.
- [ ] R1834001's title names `amended by … R4403000`, its `cards` lists R4403000, and its failing-pick paragraph points at R4403000; R4403000's `proven_in` lists both test files.
- [ ] The new `r4403000` contract test and all existing `r4403000`/`r1834001` API tests pass; no test skipped, ignored, or weakened.
- [ ] `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-server --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo jackioh spec check` are green.

## Risks

- No hermetic test can fail without this fix: the fake serializes whole transactions, so the race is unobservable under `cargo test` (the issue says the same). The contract test pins the wiring on both stores (it fails if the method is missing or reads the wrong profile); the race itself is closed by the `FOR UPDATE` text, verified by inspection and by CI's Postgres halves.
- Reject the migration alternative (applying the keep inside `app.merge_player_settings`): a new migration file would make this a migration-class change and churn checksum-pinned files for no behavioral gain; the API-layer lock is sufficient because the merge already serializes writers on the profile lock.
- Reject adding `FOR UPDATE` to the existing `player_settings_get`: it would put a write lock on the read-only `GET` route and on `loadout.rs`' seat picks. The separate method keeps the lock exactly where the filter needs it and keeps `round_trips.rs` counts unchanged.

## Open questions

None. Both findings have a settled fix above; the one honest limit (no hermetic race reproduction) is disclosed, not decided.
```
